result.title: Can Healthcare Survive Our Changing Climate?
result.description:
Climate change is a health crisis. It’s also an economic crisis.

Extreme heat, wildfire smoke, infectious diseases and drought are already affecting people's health, livelihoods and productivity.

By 2050, climate-related health impacts could contribute to at least $14.5 trillion in productivity losses across key economic sectors, according to research from the World Economic Forum's Climate and Health Initiative.

Yet health and climate finance remain fragmented, siloed and too often focused on responding to crises rather than preventing them.

What if we invested earlier — in prevention, preparedness and climate-resilient health systems?

Our new film explores what it would take to shift from reacting to climate-related health emergencies to investing in solutions that protect lives, livelihoods and economies.

The question isn't just whether we have solutions. It's whether we're prepared to finance them at the scale needed.

Featuring insights from:

Dr. Beth Thompson — @wellcometrust

Dr. Marina Romanello — @LancetCountdown

Vanina Laurent-Ledru — Institut Mérieux

Dr. Shyam Bishen — @wef

Dr. Ranit Mishori — @WorldBankGroup

Dr. Naveen Rao — @RockefellerFdn

Dr. Noubar Afeyan — @flagshippioneering

Katrín Jakobsdóttir — @who

result.title: What's taking clean energy so long?
result.description:
The energy transition began three decades ago - and yet renewables still provide just a third of global electricity and 14% of the primary energy supply.

So what’s the hold-up?

We asked four experts: Bruce Douglas of the Global Renewables Alliance, Chao Zhang of Ming Yang Smart Energy Group, Georgios Stassis of PPC and Gyanesh Chaudhary of Vikram Solar.

A new World Economic Forum report, Enabling the Electricity Era: From Proven Solutions to Execution at Scale, explores how power systems can scale fast enough to meet rapidly growing electricity demand driven by electrification, industrial growth and digital infrastructure. Read it here: https://www.weforum.org/publications/enabling-the-electricity-era-from-proven-solutions-to-execution-at-scale

result.title: The Biggest Mobility Transformation in History & What Chess Can Teach Us | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - A chess world champion explains what the game can teach us about life:
Yifan Hou is a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader. At 14, Hou became a #chess grandmaster. At 16, she became the youngest ever Women’s World Chess Champion - a record she holds to this day. Here, she explains how the game has shaped her worldview, and what it has taught her about taking on life’s challenges. 

02:52 - 3 top finance stories to know:
How worried are investors about AI-related debt? In our latest roundup of #finance and economic news, Digital editor Spencer Feingold breaks down the latest developments being tracked by the World Economic Forum's Centre for Financial and Monetary Systems. 

04:49 - We are living through the biggest mobility transformation in recorded history says FIA’s Secretary-General:
Elite cars in #F1 are showing what is possible in sustainable fuels and batteries. Elsewhere in #motorsport, a hydrogen-powered engine just posted a new land-speed record. Here, Willem Groenewald of the FIA – Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile explains what’s happening at the cutting edge - but also why it could take over a decade for the true impacts to filter down to passenger cars.

result.title: Democracies ignore the cost of living crisis at their peril - economist Isabella Weber
result.description:
Democratic governments that fail to address cost of living pressures can fuel the rise of anti-democratic forces, says Isabella Weber, Associate Professor of Economics at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. The author of the new book Anti-Fascist Economics describes the economic policies she says can ward off extremism.
